facts.text: Switch and regulator boxes are normally mounted with their bottom 1.1 m above floor level, unless directed otherwise.

Residential rooms: 6 A sockets 70 cm above floor on bed sides, otherwise 23 or 110 cm; 16 A sockets 23 or 110 cm. Kitchen: 23 cm above the working platform, away from stove and sink. Bathroom: 6 A socket at 110 cm beside the basin/mirror.

Geyser: a 16 A MCB in a modular box at 110 cm beside the bathroom switchboard or near the door, with the socket at least 2 m above floor, at least 60 cm from the shower head and within 30 cm of the geyser.
Every socket outlet is controlled by a switch or MCB on the live side, kept with the socket.
Modular socket outlets are 6 A 3-pin, 16 A 3-pin or 16/6 A 6-pin; the third pin is earthed. 2-pin and 5-pin sockets are not permitted.
A lighting circuit feeds light, fan and call-bell points, with not more than 800 W connected load or 20 points, whichever is less. LED fittings are rated as per actuals.
A residential power circuit feeds not more than two 16 A outlets, or three 6 A outlets, or one 16 A and two 6 A outlets. Geyser, AC, oven and washing-machine outlets each get an independent circuit.
Lights, fans and call bells are wired in lighting circuits; 6 A and 16 A socket outlets are wired in power circuits.
Power wiring is kept separate from light wiring from the circuit level; conduits for light and power wiring are separate.
For design, conventional ceiling fans are rated at 60 W; 6 A and 16 A socket points at 100 W and 1000 W unless actual loads are specified.
Copper conductors only; minimum 1.5 mm² for light wiring and 4.0 mm² for power wiring; circuits above 1 kW sized by calculation.
Colour code: phases red/yellow/blue in three-phase wiring; live red in single-phase wiring; neutral black; earth yellow/green.
No break in the neutral except in linked switchgear; control switches are on the live side.
A circuit (phase, neutral, earth) terminates in the first switchboard on phase, neutral and earth connector blocks, from which point wiring starts.
DBs have incoming and outgoing terminal blocks, pre-wired, with a phase/neutral/earth terminal block for each circuit (or an approved loose-wire box with terminal blocks).
The main board of a dwelling is an MCB board with an ELCB (RCD) with the incoming MCB, double-door, in a ventilated niche in the room connecting to the entry.
Switchboards are located in common areas such as corridors or lobbies, in dry ventilated spaces, not above a gas stove or sink, and not in bathrooms, toilets or kitchens.
RCCBs in household installations have a rated tripping current not exceeding 30 mA.
Arc fault detection devices (AFDDs) are to be used for protection against arc-fault fire in households, per IS 17121.
Three-phase circuits are balanced.
Minimum conduit size 20 mm. Cables per conduit (bends present): 20 mm takes 4 × 1.5 mm² or 2 × 4 mm²; 25 mm takes 8 × 1.5 mm² or 5 × 4 mm².
Conduit bends have a radius of at least 7.5 cm, and no length of conduit has more than the equivalent of four quarter-bends from outlet to outlet.

Conduits in RCC work are tied to the reinforcement before concreting, with long-radius bends; inspection boxes are flush with the ceiling concrete and at least 65 mm deep in roof slabs; box locations are marked.
Conduits are buried in neat wall chases before plastering and fixed by saddles not more than 60 cm apart (and 15 cm either side of a bend for PVC).
Outgoing and return cables are bunched in the same conduit.

A protective (earth) conductor is drawn inside the conduit of every circuit and terminated on the earth terminal of each switch box and the earth terminal block of the DB; gas or water pipes are never used as protective conductors.
Conduits are generally not taken in floor slabs; wiring passing through walls or floors is sleeved and openings are sealed.
Switch boxes are metal (GI for modular) or IS 14772 PVC, at least 60 mm clear depth, with an earth terminal (stud, washers, terminal block) in every metal box; regulator boxes are metal.
Modular control switches are ON when the knob is down.

Fans are wired to a ceiling rose or connector box and hung from a hook with an insulator; on RCC roofs a 12 mm MS U-rod is bound to the top reinforcement; the canopy hides the suspension; lead-in wire at least 1.5 mm²; two-module step-type electronic regulators are recommended.

A ceiling fan is controlled through its own regulator and a switch in series; its lowest point is at least 2.4 m above floor and its blade plane at least 300 mm below the ceiling. (CPWD 3.16.1(p) hangs fans at 2.75 m unless specified.)
Indicative fan size and number by room width and length (e.g. 4 × 4 m: one 1200 mm fan; 4 × 6 m: two 1200 mm fans).
The metallic body of a fan regulator is connected to earth by a protective conductor.
An exhaust fan is fixed in a wall opening and connected by flexible cord to an exhaust-fan point wired as near the opening as possible.
Earth electrodes are at least 1.5 m from the building and at least 3 m apart; the earthing conductor is buried at least 0.5 m deep.
Before energising: continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, earth-fault loop impedance, RCD, functional and voltage-drop tests.
The use of electricity in an installation is controlled by a residual current device; in domestic installations its residual operating current does not exceed 30 mA.

The supplier provides an earthed terminal near the point of commencement of supply; for installations above 250 V the consumer also provides an own earthing system with an independent electrode, interlinked with that terminal through a suitable link.
Apparatus above 250 V is earthed by two separate and distinct connections; earth-fault loop impedance must let the protective device disconnect in time.
The consumer fits a switch-fuse unit or circuit breaker as near as possible after the point of commencement of supply; every circuit has its own fuse or circuit breaker.
No cut-out, link, switch or circuit breaker other than a linked switch (operating with the live conductors) is inserted in the earthed neutral.
A clear space of not less than one metre is provided in front of a switchboard; non-metallic conduit is permitted up to 650 V.
Installations above 250 V carry a danger notice.

Consumer meters are generally owned by the licensee and installed at the premises or outside, easily accessible; new connections get smart (prepayment) meters; the consumer provides earth-leakage protection; only the licensee seals or unseals the meter.

facts.text: Single-phase LT supply is limited to about 10 kW (Delhi), 40 A (Maharashtra), 5 kW (Karnataka, Kerala, Uttar Pradesh) or 4 kW connected load (Tamil Nadu); larger domestic loads get three-phase four-wire supply.
Distribution transformers step 11 kV down to 433 V three-phase; nominal LV supply is 230 V phase-to-neutral / 400 V phase-to-phase at 50 Hz (some state codes still state 240/415 V).
A distribution board is fixed not higher than 2 m, with about 1 m clear space in front.
Fit the energy meter first, then the main switch and DB; the meter is preferably not below 1 m.
Concealed conduits are laid over the slab reinforcement before concreting and dropped in wall chases to DB and switch boxes; draw wires are pulled through completed conduits.

Easy9 Plus TPN boards have knockouts on top and bottom, a removable centre plate (dead front), a door that hinges left or right, vertical neutral and earth bars at the sides, and 12 mm strip length at 1.5 N·m.

Easy9 TPN double-door 8-way: 422 × 471 × 90 mm, 8 incomer + 24 outgoing modules. SPN double-door 8-way: 224 × 293 × 93 mm. 1P MCB 18 mm wide; 4P RCCB and 4P isolator 72 mm wide; device height about 81 mm.
Three-pin sockets have the earth contact above two current-carrying contacts; terminals are marked L, N and earth.
Approximate overall diameters: 1.5 mm² about 3.0 mm; 2.5 mm² about 3.4–3.6 mm; 4 mm² about 4.2 mm.
Rigid PVC conduit outside diameters 20 mm and 25 mm (light, medium and heavy wall classes).

assumptions.title: Three-phase, four-wire LT service (assumed)
assumptions.text: The simulation assumes a 230/400 V, 50 Hz three-phase four-wire low-voltage service from a local 11 kV/433 V distribution transformer. The architectural project contains no sanctioned load or DISCOM data. Using CPWD design ratings, the modelled points total about 9.3 kW before LED lighting is added. That is above the single-phase limit in Tamil Nadu (4 kW), Karnataka, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh (5 kW) and Maharashtra (40 A), and close to Delhi's 10 kW. Three-phase is therefore a reasonable assumption for this model, not a verified fact about the property.
assumptions.confirm: DISCOM connection approval and the consumer's sanctioned load

assumptions.title: Earthing arrangement not determined
assumptions.text: CEA Reg. 18 requires a consumer's own earth electrode for installations above 250 V, interlinked with the supplier's earthed terminal; Reg. 43 asks for two distinct connections. The simulation shows two electrodes, a main earthing terminal at the main DB earth bar and a protective-earth conductor in every circuit. The supplier's earthed terminal, the interlink and whether the arrangement behaves as TN-C-S or TT are not determined here, so no neutral–earth link is drawn. The 30 mA RCCB (CEA Reg. 44) gives earth-leakage protection either way.
assumptions.confirm: Licensed electrical designer, DISCOM and electrical inspector

assumptions.title: Meter outside the entry room
assumptions.text: One sealed DISCOM three-phase meter in a meter box on the outside face of the entry room's external side wall, back-to-back with the main DB and readable from the open side yard, fed by an underground service cable (route beyond the plot not shown). The DISCOM decides the actual location and enclosure.

assumptions.title: Main DB in the entry room
assumptions.text: A double-door TPN MCB DB (scaled on Schneider Easy9 EZ9ETND08) flush in the entry room wall, back-to-back with the meter, with a 4-pole incoming MCB and a 4-pole 30 mA RCCB as CPWD 3.20.9 describes. Its outgoing P/N/E terminal blocks are in a loose-wire box above it (CPWD 3.18.2, Fig. 8).
assumptions.confirm: Electrical designer (device ratings, IP rating, discrimination)

assumptions.title: Single-phase first-floor sub-DB
assumptions.text: The first floor is served from one phase through a double-pole-isolated SPN sub-DB (scaled on EZ9ESND08) in the first-floor common area, fed by a submain from an outgoing MCB in the main DB. Its circuits are covered by the main 30 mA RCCB; a designer may instead add a separate RCD for better continuity of supply.

assumptions.title: Circuit grouping and phase allocation are illustrative
assumptions.text: Rooms are grouped into lighting circuits of at most 12 points (within CPWD's 20-point limit) and power circuits within CPWD 3.10.3. Every circuit serving one room is on one phase, so no two phases appear in the same room. Phases are balanced on CPWD design ratings; LED wattages are unknown and are not added.
assumptions.confirm: Electrical designer (load schedule, diversity, cable sizing)

assumptions.title: Concealed routes are generated, not surveyed
assumptions.text: Conduits run in the RCC slab above each storey (laid before concreting) and drop vertically in wall chases to boxes. Routes avoid slab openings and long horizontal wall chases. Actual routes depend on beams, reinforcement, sunken slabs and site conditions.
assumptions.confirm: Electrical designer and structural engineer; site survey

assumptions.title: Conventional ceiling fans with step regulators
assumptions.text: Fan points are proposed at room positions clear of downlights. The simulation assumes conventional (non-BLDC) fans with 2-module step regulators in series after the fan switch. Only the installation conductors to the fan's connector are shown — not the fan's internal motor wiring. A BLDC or remote-controlled fan would bypass the regulator.

assumptions.title: Device ratings are not designed
assumptions.text: MCB, RCCB and isolator current ratings, conductor sizes above CPWD minimums, submain size and fault levels are not calculated here, and are shown as 'by designer'.

assumptions.title: Positions are proposals
assumptions.text: Light positions come from the architectural scene. Fan, socket, switchboard and DB positions are proposed from clear wall spans, door swings and furniture in the copied model.
assumptions.confirm: Electrical designer and owner; site measurement

assumptions.title: Water-heater positions assumed
assumptions.text: The architectural model has no water heaters. Each bathroom's geyser socket is placed where a wall-hung heater could reasonably go; the heater itself is not drawn.

assumptions.title: Colours follow CPWD 3.5.5
assumptions.text: Final circuits are single-phase, so their live and switched conductors are red; the incoming service cores are red/yellow/blue/black. The engineering overlay (amber selection, cyan trace) is separate from the physical insulation colours.
assumptions.confirm: Site practice may differ; check IS 732:2019 and the contract specification

G1.title: Supply arrives at the sealed meter
G1.text: The DISCOM's underground service cable rises inside the external wall into the back of the meter box. The meter belongs to the licensee and stays sealed; the incoming cable is live even when the house main switch is off.

G1.title: Meter tails reach the main DB
G1.text: Four meter tails (R, Y, B, N) pass through a sleeve in the wall into the main DB, behind the meter.

G1.title: Main switch and 30 mA RCCB
G1.text: The 4-pole incoming MCB isolates and protects the whole installation (CEA Reg. 37). The 4-pole RCCB compares the currents in R, Y, B and N and trips on a residual (earth-leakage) current of 30 mA (CEA Reg. 44).

G1.title: G1 MCB on the R phase
G1.text: The single-pole MCB for G1 sits on the R-phase tooth of the busbar and opens only the phase conductor. Its neutral returns through the RCCB's neutral bar and is never switched (CEA Reg. 17).

G1.title: Outgoing P/N/E terminal blocks
G1.text: G1 leaves from its own phase, neutral and earth terminal blocks in the loose-wire box (CPWD 3.18.2).

G1.title: Concealed run to the Modular kitchen switchboard
G1.text: Phase, neutral and protective conductor run together in one PVC conduit (CPWD 5.4.3(g), 5.4.4): up a wall chase, through the RCC slab (laid before concreting) and down a chase to the next box.

G1.title: Modular kitchen switchboard
G1.text: The circuit lands on phase, neutral and earth connector blocks in this box (CPWD 3.5.6); point wiring starts here. Open the plate to see the terminals.

G1.title: Ceiling lights 1 of 2 (2) switch
G1.text: The switch interrupts only the live conductor (CPWD 3.11.5); the neutral goes straight to the point.

G1.title: Point wiring through the slab
G1.text: From the board the switched live, neutral and protective conductor rise in a wall chase, then run in the slab through 1 intermediate point box to the point. Neutral and earth are looped at each box; only this point's live is switched.

G1.title: Modular kitchen · Ceiling light
G1.text: Light point box above the downlight: switched live, neutral and protective conductor.
